rationale: B wins because it refuses the fake bridge A keeps flirting with. A's lead, "Its Avocado Robot Explains Why," overclaims causality the update does not prove; B names the cleaner story, "Chipotle says it won't raise prices this year," then immediately asks whether the automation link is real. B has fewer angles, but they are cleaner, sharper, and less likely to hand a reporter a correction wrapped in guacamole.
gaps_in_A: "Its Avocado Robot Explains Why" is too causal for the facts. The update says the price hold and robot rollout are simultaneous; it does not say Autocado funds the price hold.
"Chipotle Says Its Robots Justify Flat Prices" repeats the same unsupported bridge in investor clothing. The caveat is good, but the headline still sells the claim too hard.
"Competitors Are Taking Notes" is an invented reaction. No competitor response or evidence of competitor attention appears in the update.
Four angles creates some padding: the consumer-prices and investor-margin angles are structurally close because both depend on the same missing savings math.
gaps_in_B: "Food robotics has been stuck in pilot-program purgatory" is a broad category claim that needs outside support. It may be true, but it is not in the update.
"100 stores is the pilot-to-deployment threshold this beat watches for" sounds like an invented industry threshold. Useful framing, but it needs sourcing before it survives contact with a reporter.
The first angle could make more of the 100-store Autocado rollout as context, even while refusing to claim it funds the price hold.
